## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Curves shapes
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Evaluating plane arcs, function graphs, and polynomial pieces
//  - Evaluating the polar and figure curves
//  - Evaluating the plane spirals and roulettes
//  - Evaluating the named space curves

library CurvesShapes
{
    //==
    // # Evaluating plane arcs, function graphs, and polynomial pieces
    //
    // Closed-form evaluation of the types declared in `curves-shapes.types.plato`, plus
    // the two angle-to-point helpers (CirclePoint, RotateBy) that every circular,
    // polar, and roulette formula in the curves-2d family is written against.
    //
    // Conventions:
    //   * The canonical curve parameter is `t` in [0, 1] (the `IProcedural` domain
    //     inherited through `ICurve2D`).
    //   * Types carrying an `Angles: AngleInterval` sweep map t through
    //     `Angles.Lerp(t)`; types without one map t to `t.Turns`, one full
    //     revolution, as `curves.concepts.plato` documents for
    //     `IPolarCurve2D`.

    //==
    // # Shared helpers

    // The displacement of length `radius` at the given angle from +X:
    // (radius * cos theta, radius * sin theta). The angle-to-point evaluator
    // under every circular, polar, and roulette formula below.
    CirclePoint(theta: Angle, radius: Number): Vector2D
        => (theta.Cos * radius, theta.Sin * radius);

    // The vector rotated counter-clockwise by the given angle.
    RotateBy(v: Vector2D, angle: Angle): Vector2D
        => (v.X * angle.Cos - v.Y * angle.Sin,
                    v.X * angle.Sin + v.Y * angle.Cos);

    //==
    // # Arcs and conic pieces

    // The point at the swept angle on the circle of radius Radius about Center.
    Eval(self: CircularArc2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => self.Center + self.Angles.Lerp(t).CirclePoint(self.Radius);

    // The point at the swept parametric angle on the ellipse: the axis-aligned
    // point (a cos theta, b sin theta) tilted by Rotation and placed at Center.
    Eval(self: EllipticalArc2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => self.Center
         + Vector2D(self.Radii.X * self.Angles.Lerp(t).Cos,
                    self.Radii.Y * self.Angles.Lerp(t).Sin).RotateBy(self.Rotation);

    // The point (x, Coefficient * x^2) with x swept over Domain.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parabola
    Eval(self: Parabola2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => (self.Domain.Lerp(t), self.Coefficient * self.Domain.Lerp(t).Square);

    //==
    // # Function graphs

    // The point (x, Scale * cosh(x / Scale)) with x swept over Domain. The
    // hyperbolic cosine is only declared on Angle, so the ratio is cast with
    // the radians constructor before Cosh.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catenary
    Eval(self: Catenary2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => (self.Domain.Lerp(t),
                   self.Scale * (self.Domain.Lerp(t) / self.Scale).Angle.Cosh);

    // The point (x, Amplitude * sin(2*pi*x/Wavelength + Phase)) with x swept
    // over Domain. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sine_wave
    Eval(self: SineCurve2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => (self.Domain.Lerp(t),
                   self.Amplitude
                   * ((self.Domain.Lerp(t) / self.Wavelength).Turns + self.Phase).Sin);

    //==
    // # Polynomial arcs
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9zier_curve
    // The Bernstein forms live in `library Polynomials` (polynomials.types.plato),
    // generic over `INumerical`; control points are converted to displacements
    // with PositionVector and the result back with ToPoint.

    // The quadratic Bezier point at t.
    Eval(self: QuadraticBezier2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => self.P0.PositionVector
               .QuadraticBezier(self.P1.PositionVector, self.P2.PositionVector, t)
               .ToPoint;

    // The cubic Bezier point at t.
    Eval(self: CubicBezier2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => self.P0.PositionVector
               .CubicBezier(self.P1.PositionVector, self.P2.PositionVector,
                            self.P3.PositionVector, t)
               .ToPoint;

    // The IDeformable2D obligation: every control point carried through the
    // mapping. Exact for an affine mapping, which commutes with the Bernstein
    // basis; under a nonlinear one the result is the Bezier over the moved
    // control points, not the image of the curve.
    Deform(self: QuadraticBezier2D, mapping: Function1<Point2D, Point2D>): QuadraticBezier2D
        => (mapping(self.P0), mapping(self.P1), mapping(self.P2));

    // The IDeformable2D obligation: every control point carried through the mapping.
    Deform(self: CubicBezier2D, mapping: Function1<Point2D, Point2D>): CubicBezier2D
        => (mapping(self.P0), mapping(self.P1), mapping(self.P2), mapping(self.P3));

    //==
    // # Evaluating the polar and figure curves
    //
    // Closed-form evaluation of the types declared in `curves-shapes.types.plato`, plus
    // the generic `IPolarCurve2D` bridge that turns a `RadiusAt` into a position for
    // every polar implementor in the tree. The shared `CirclePoint` helper is in
    // the arcs section above.
    //
    // Conventions:
    //   * The canonical curve parameter is `t` in [0, 1] (the `IProcedural` domain
    //     inherited through `ICurve2D`).
    //   * `IPolarCurve2D` implementors only need `RadiusAt`. The generic
    //     `Eval(IPolarCurve2D, Number)` below turns that into a position, so the
    //     polar zoo costs one line per curve.

    //==
    // # IPolarCurve2D — the generic bridge
    //
    // A polar curve is fully determined by RadiusAt, so its Eval is derivable
    // once for every implementor. Curves that carry an explicit `Angles` sweep
    // override this with their own Eval below.

    // The position at the canonical parameter t: the polar radius taken at
    // t full turns, converted to Cartesian.
    Eval(self: IPolarCurve2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => self.CartesianPositionAt(t.Turns);

    //==
    // # Polar and figure curves

    // r = Radius * cos(k * theta).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_(mathematics)
    RadiusAt(self: RoseCurve2D, angle: Angle): Number
        => self.Radius * (angle * self.PetalFrequency).Cos;

    // r = 2 * Radius * (1 + cos theta), over one full turn.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardioid
    Eval(self: Cardioid2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => t.Turns.CirclePoint(2.0 * self.Radius * (1.0 + t.Turns.Cos)).ToPoint;

    // r = Offset + Amplitude * cos theta, over one full turn.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lima%C3%A7on
    Eval(self: Limacon2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => t.Turns.CirclePoint(self.Offset + self.Amplitude * t.Turns.Cos).ToPoint;

    // r = sqrt(Scale^2 * cos(2 theta)), over one full turn. The radius is
    // imaginary on the quadrants where cos(2 theta) is negative; those
    // parameters lie off the real curve.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lemniscate_of_Bernoulli
    Eval(self: Lemniscate2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => t.Turns.CirclePoint((self.Scale.Square * (t.Turns * 2.0).Cos).Sqrt).ToPoint;
```
